changes.place: Sphere contours, equator and point positions
changes.h: une sphère avec son équateur portant deux points, un troisième point au-dessus
changes.ink: The pencil outline is retraced on the right, and an additional open curve runs outside the left edge and above the equator. The front equator is a shallow bowed arc; the two dark points are on it, with the third above it. These separate strokes and their placement are retained rather than collapsed into two regular ellipses.

changes.place: Bipyramid edges, marked positions and retracing
changes.h: une bipyramide à base quadrilatère dont les sommets sont marqués
changes.ink: The top, left, back and right marks have visible hollow centres; the front lower mark is dark and tapered. Several edges stop short of a marked position or run in parallel. The lower left edges fan into distinct retraced strokes, with a small loop farther down-left. The central bottom meeting overlaps printed zeros, so no clean extra circular marker is imposed there.

changes.place: Right open oval and associated strokes
changes.h: plus à droite, un ovale à peine visible.
changes.ink: The figure has two distinct left-side curves, an open right-hand end, and a slanted branch passing through a small angular mark on its upper-left side. C’s single lower arrow curve omits these contours and puts an arrowhead at a different endpoint.

changes.place: Possible pi inside the right oval
changes.ink: A short dark sloping top stroke is followed by a hooked left descender and a much lighter right descender. This admits the reading pi, but the small shape could also be angular drawing strokes. C’s doubt is retained; the mark is not silently omitted under H’s description as without text.

changes.ink: All 32 rows are dark front-side printing. After rotating the saved crop by 180 degrees the letters are normally oriented: GUTS OUTPUT FOR PREDONT DELIVER AT 0000 - PREDONT.MODULEF5. Each row has four zeros, the short separator, a period after PREDONT, and final F5. Pencil strokes across the last upright rows are drawing overlaps, not typed substitutions or cancellations.

The first digit has two open rightward bowls; the second has a long upright with an angled approach at its head. The digits read 31. Their attribution is unassigned, so the same reading is retained as a margin foliation.

decisions.ink: A dark sloping horizontal top and hooked left descender are visible, with a faint right descender. The figure does not distinguish a letter pi from small angular drawing strokes. The existing doubt remains.

notes.text: The main pencil drawing consists of a sphere with three marked points, a bipyramid-like figure with retraced edges, and an open oval to its right. Relative positions, hollow centres and dark marks are retained in TikZ.
The possible pi in the right oval remains doubtful. No map or other mathematical role is inferred from the letter-shaped mark.

The front-side printer block contains 32 identical rows, each reading GUTS OUTPUT FOR PREDONT DELIVER AT 0000 - PREDONT.MODULEF5. It is upside down relative to the pencil sketches and is set with that orientation. It is not the pale mirrored printing seen through other reused sheets.

The peripheral pale blue-gray oval groups are reverse-side impressions, not additional front drawings. Their broken contours differ from the continuous pencil strokes. Root independently reported mirrored positional matches with drawings on the opposite side: the middle group with scan031 II1, the lower-left group with scan031 III2-prime right sphere, the upper groups with I4/I6, and the lower-middle group with III2-prime left sphere. Reader B did not open scan031.

Several lower pencil lines cross the dark printer text. These are retained as drawing overlaps; no printed word is treated as deleted or replaced. The crowded lower junction remains only approximately drawable.
Foliation 31 is clear, but its hand is unassigned. H omits both this number and the printer block. No mathematical claim on the sheet was independently checked.

differences_review.review: H’s description of the physical sheet is editorial. The dark normally oriented printing after 180-degree rotation is front-side text and remains in full.
The sphere and all three marked points are transcribed as strokes and points, not by importing H’s prose synopsis.
The central figure is traced from its actual edges and marks. A regular clean lower circled apex is not imposed where pencil and print overlap.
The front right oval is retained. Peripheral pale broken oval groups are excluded as reverse-side impressions; H’s editorial prose is not manuscript text.
All main drawing details and all 32 printer rows were compared. The printer block and foliation are retained despite H’s omission; the possible pi stays doubtful.

reading_procedure.display_encoding: The PNG half delivery was rejected before display; each half was then viewed once as a native-dimension JPEG. Evidence PNGs remain unchanged; final crop display JPEGs use quality85.
